title: The Ferrofluidic Liquid Metal Revolution: Breaking the 10 kW/cm2 Thermal Wall with Electromagnetically Actuated Jet Impingement for AI Chips and EV Inverters
content: This comprehensive review paper examines three interconnected domains that represent the forefront of thermal engineering challenges in the 21st century: electronic cooling, data center thermal management, and electric vehicle battery and powertrain thermal systems. As power densities continue to escalate across all three domains — driven by miniaturi-zation in consumer electronics, explosive growth in cloud computing and artificial intel-ligence workloads, and the global transition to electrified transportation — the effective dissipation of heat has emerged as a critical bottleneck constraining performance, reliabil-ity, and energy efficiency. This paper systematically reviews fundamental heat transfer mechanisms, state-of-the-art cooling technologies, emerging materials and architectures, and the evolving regulatory and sustainability landscape. Key findings indicate that two-phase immersion cooling, advanced heat pipe systems, microchannel heat exchang-ers, and phase change materials are among the most promising near-term solutions. Long-term advances hinge on the integration of intelligent thermal management systems leveraging machine learning, novel nanofluids, and topology-optimized heat sink de-signs. The convergence of these technologies across sectors presents unique cross-disciplinary opportunities and is expected to define the trajectory of thermal engi-neering research through 2035 and beyond.
